input:
Edge case: GICv4.2 vNMI delivery to a vPE that is NOT currently scheduled. The host has the vPE in 'unscheduled' state in the ITS VPENDBASER register.

Per the GICv4.2 architecture spec: 
  - Pending bit is set in vPE's pending table
  - When vPE is later scheduled (VMOVP), vNMI fires
  - Latency between physical NMI source and vNMI delivery =     schedule latency (potentially milliseconds)

Is this acceptable for a hard-real-time vNMI watchdog? What pinning strategy (vCPU-to-pCPU affinity) eliminates schedule latency? When should the system fall back to direct NMI delivery to the host (vs vNMI)?
